description: Maximum clique cardinality using approximate-coloring bounds with selectively recomputed degree order.

source.title: An Improved Branch and Bound Algorithm for the Maximum Clique Problem
source.reference: MATCH Communications in Mathematical and in Computer Chemistry 58(3), pp. 569-590, Section 2
source.algorithm_attribution: Clean-room bounded MaxCliqueDyn-style approximate coloring, branch-and-bound, and dynamic degree reordering; algorithm descriptions only.

input.adjacency_mask_range: nonnegative masks with bits only in [0,n)
input.graph: simple undirected and loopless; each row mask is symmetric with its opposite row

workspace.meaning: Fixed adjacency rows, candidate/color-order arrays in recursion frames of depth at most 24, current clique, dynamic step counters, and bounded call-frame allowance.

contract.root_order: Initialize all vertices by descending degree, with ascending vertex ID as the deterministic tie break; assign each suffix the bound min(position, maximum_degree)+1.
contract.candidate_order: For each selected vertex, intersect the earlier candidate prefix with its neighborhood, greedily partition that list into independent color classes, and visit the concatenated classes from the highest color down.
contract.dynamic_reordering: At each nonempty child candidate set, update the per-depth search count and total coloring-call count. Recompute descending-degree order when 1000*prior_depth_count < 25*new_total_count, matching the 0.025 threshold; ascending vertex ID breaks degree ties.
contract.color_bound: A color class is an independent set, so its one-based color number bounds the size of a clique in that candidate suffix. Drop colors below max(best-current_size+1,1).
contract.validation: Reject negative or out-of-domain masks, self loops, asymmetric adjacency, truncated rows, and trailing words.

oracle_method: The primary reference applies MaxCliqueDyn-style dynamic degree reordering and greedy coloring bounds. The independent reference enumerates vertex subsets and checks pairwise adjacency; it is used through 16 vertices. The 24-vertex path and complete graph have hand-derived answers and are checked against the primary only.
